flags.reason: Health-threat warning given without permission; pushes rather than exploring her reasons (sustain talk at line 27).
Same advice repeated five times (lines 11, 16, 24, 41, 47) despite resistance; ignores participant's stated preferences.
Sustain talk 'maybe after the summer' met with brief reflection; no exploration of ambivalence or importance.
Fridge reminder and day plan (lines 42, 44) were not reinforced or explored; coach moved to repeating advice.
'You figured that out on your own' praises something the participant did not do; undermines trust.

score.summary: The coach asked good open questions and reached a concrete goal with a barrier plan, but repeated the same walking advice five times and used a health-threat warning that pushed against the participant's stated reluctance. Susan's change talk (fridge reminder, Mon/Wed/Fri plan, bigger lunch) was not reinforced, and her feelings and next contact were never addressed.
strengths: Line 30: complex reflection names both sides of Susan's ambivalence about the rain and her wish to succeed.
Line 52: 'What might get in the way?' prepared her for barriers and produced a concrete plan (line 53).
Line 54: clear summary before closing, with her confirmation at line 55.
coaching_tips: Line 16/24/41/47: Stop repeating the same walking advice after the first offer; ask what she thinks of it instead.
Line 28: Replace the health warning with an open question like 'What worries you most about your health right now?'
Line 42/44: Reinforce her fridge reminder and Mon/Wed/Fri plan with a reflection or affirmation, then ask how she'll use them.
Line 36: Explore 'after the summer' with a complex reflection or a question about what would make it feel worth starting sooner.
Line 7: Avoid praising things the participant did not do; affirm her actual effort instead.
